jobs.description:
Empowering Wellness, Transforming Lives

Optima Medical Management Group is dedicated to enhancing the quality of life by promoting wellness. At Optima MMG and all of its divisions: Serene Health, Community Support, and American TrueCare, our mission is to provide comprehensive support and care that not only addresses immediate concerns but also fosters long-term well-being.

As pioneers in the field, we aspire to lead in member care outcomes and set new standards for excellence and innovation. We are committed to empowering our members to achieve self-sufficiency in health, creating a ripple effect that strengthens families and communities.

Our work culture at Optima MMG is built on pride, passion, and a collective commitment to making a positive difference in people's lives. Our team members are dedicated problem-solvers who bring their unique skills and perspectives to the table. We believe that by fostering a collaborative and supportive environment, we can unlock the full potential of our team and, in turn, provide the best possible care to our members.

A career at Optima MMG is an opportunity to be part of a dynamic and forward-thinking organization. We encourage continuous learning and professional growth, providing our employees with access to industry experts, cutting-edge technologies, and a supportive community that values each individual's contributions. Join us on this journey to not only advance your career but to be a driving force in transforming lives and communities through passionate and fulfilling work!

This job is temporarily hybrid/ remote. Please see travel details at the bottom.

Job Summary:

The official job title is Lead Care Manager (LCM). 

The Lead Care Manager (LCM) role involves developing personalized care plans, coordinating member services, and collaborating closely with members and families, as well as Primary Care Providers to ensure they receive necessary medical treatment and support. The LCM will consult with members to determine their needs, develop individualized action plans, and work with care teams to manage the member experience effectively. Providing emotional support, resolving administrative issues, and ensuring timely access to care are key aspects of the position. Compassion, healthcare knowledge, and exceptional customer service are essential qualities for assisting members in becoming self-sufficient in health. The LCM will work with a diverse population of members enrolled in the Enhanced Care Management program, which may involve one or multiple members from the population of focus section below.

Responsibilities:

Interview members to assess medical and social determinant of healthcare gaps and provide education about their condition and medication, while developing individualized care plans.
Respond to member inquiries and concerns, ensuring adherence to hospital and legal requirements.
Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams, locate medical and social resources, and coordinate social service plans.
Maintain on-going contact with members, via telehealth and in-person visitation.
Advocate for members, consult with healthcare providers, arrange appointments and treatment plans, evaluate member progress, and assist with healthcare barriers.
Maintain empathy and professionalism while contacting members and families.
Supporting behavioral health coordination, Substance Abuse and Community Resources.
Perform additional duties as assigned.

Populations of Focus:

Individuals experiencing homelessness: Lacking a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence.
Individuals at risk for avoidable hospital or emergency department utilization: Five or more emergency room visits in a six-month period that could have been avoided with appropriate outpatient care or improved treatment adherence.
Individuals with Serious Mental Health and/ or substance use disorder needs: Adults who meet the eligibility criteria for participation in, or obtaining services through Specialist mental health services or the Drug Medi-Cal organized delivery system or Drug Medi-Cal program.
Individuals transitioning from incarceration/Justice Involved: Adults transitioning from a correctional setting or transitioned from a correction setting within the past 12 months, or children and youth who are transitioning from a youth correctional facility or transitioned from being in a youth correctional facility within the past 12 months.
Adults living in the community and at risk for long-term care institutionalization: Adults who are living in the community who meet the SNF Level of Care criteria; or who require lower-acuity skilled nursing or equipment for prevention, diagnosis, or treatment of acute illness or injury.
Adult nursing facility residents transitioning to the community: Adult nursing residents who are interested in moving out of the institution, and are likely candidates to do so successfully, and are able to reside continuously in the community.
Children and youth enrolled in California Children’s Services (CCS) or CCS Whole Child Model (WCM) with Additional Needs Beyond the CCS condition: Children and youth enrolled in CCS or CCS WCM and are experiencing at least one complex social factor influencing their health.
Children and Youth Involved in Child Welfare
Individuals with Intellectual/ Developmental Disabilities: Adults who have a diagnosed I/ DD and qualify for eligibility in any other adult ECM population of focus.
Pregnant and Postpartum individuals; Birth Equity Population of Focus: Adults and youth who are pregnant or postpartum and qualify for eligibility in any other adult or youth ECM POF, or are subject to racial and ethnic disparities.

Education and Experience:

High school diploma or GED required.
Minimum of 1 year experience in case management, member care, customer service, call center, or member care required.
Valid California driver's license and valid vehicle insurance required.
MA certificate or medical terminology knowledge preferred.

Required Skills/Abilities:

Excellent communication, interpersonal, customer service and organizational skills.
Bilingual in Spanish (Required).
Computer skills for documentation, email and chat support.
Proficient skills in working independently and collaboratively in a team to provide member care.
Proficiency in multitasking, organization, and attention to detail is required for effectively providing care to multiple members simultaneously.
Candidates should exhibit the capability to utilize resources effectively for problem-solving while maintaining composure under pressure in a compassionate manner.
Applicants must demonstrate proficient speaking, reading, and typing abilities and possess strong proofreading skills.

Physical Requirements:

Must be able to travel using personal vehicle to complete outreach visits. Mileage reimbursement for the use of your vehicle is at a standard rate.
Must successfully complete and maintain current Tuberculosis (TB) testing and clearance in accordance with company policy and applicable local/state health regulations as a condition of employment.
Prolonged periods of sitting at an office desk on the computer.
Lifting: Able to lift up to 15lbs.

Travel Details:

First week of employment will report to the Cerritos office.
Mileage reimbursement is compensated at the IRS standard rate.
Commute to the Cerritos office is considered work time. Staff member can leave their home at the start of their scheduled shift.
LCM will report to the Cerritos office twice a month during the first month of employment.
After the first month the staff member will be evaluated on the frequencies of office visits.
Office visits will decrease to once per month based on the needs of the office.

Pay range: $25 USD - $28 USD

Benefits

Our full-time employees are eligible for the following benefits enrollment after 60 days of employment:

Medical, Dental, & Vision Benefits: We have various insurance options for you and your family.

Short & Long-Term Disability Benefits: Protection when you need it most.

Voluntary Accident, Voluntary Critical Illness, and Voluntary Hospital Indemnity Plans: Added security for you and your loved ones.

Flexible Spending Accounts: Manage your finances with flexibility.

Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Support when life throws challenges your way.

401(K): Building your financial future with us. Effective after 1 year of employment.

Paid Vacation and Sick Leave: Flexibility for the planned and unplanned.

Paid Holidays: Quality time to enjoy celebrations.

Employee Referral Program: Share the opportunities and reap the rewards.

Company Discount Program: Enjoy savings on everyday expenses and memberships.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Optima Medical Management Group and its divisions are an Equal Opportunity Employer. Optima MMG is committed to providing employment opportunities for all qualified candidates without discrimination on the basis of race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. Optima MMG is committed to providing reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities.

Pre-Employment

Optima Medical Management Group is a drug-free workplace. Employment is contingent upon a successful pre-employment drug screening and background check.

We’re also home to notable specialty programs, including cancer care, heart surgery, orthopedic surgery, labor and delivery services (including a Level III neonatal intensive care unit) and a nationally designated Comprehensive Stroke Center.

This is a Full-Time (70 hours per pay period, every two weeks) position with 10.25-hour shifts on variable days of the week. Position requires working every other full weekend and rotating holidays.

Located at Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla.

Join the Scripps Health team and work alongside passionate caregivers and provide patient-centered healthcare. Receive endless appreciation while you build a rewarding career with one of the most respected healthcare organizations nationwide.

Why join Scripps Health?

At Scripps Health, your ambition is empowered and your abilities are appreciated:

Nearly a quarter of our employees have been with Scripps Health for over 10 years.
Scripps is a Great Place to Work Certified company for 2026
Scripps Health has been consistently ranked as a top employer for women, millennials, diversity, and as an overall workplace by various national publications.
Beckers Healthcare ranked Scripps Health on its 2026 list of 150 top places to work in health care.
We have transitional and professional development programs to create a learning environment that enables you to thrive in your specific field as well as in your overall career.
Our specialties have been nationally recognized for quality in areas such as cardiovascular care, oncology, orthopedics, geriatrics, obstetrics and gynecology, and gastroenterology.

Established in 1924 by Ellen Browning Scripps, Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla has been one of Southern California’s premier medical centers for more than 90 years. Scripps La Jolla was ranked No. 1 by U.S. News and World Report U.S. News for the San Diego region and among the best in the nation in eight specialties.

We invite you to join our highly engaged Scripps Memorial La Jolla Hospital Case Management team.

As a Case Manager you will be responsible for the daily management and coordination of care for patients in the hospital with identified immediate skilled post-acute care needs including coordination with providers, navigators and ancillary and community resources across the system and care continuum. Addresses payer issues that impact care, develops a transition plan of care from inpatient to post-acute that includes a safe discharge plan.
Ensures that the patient/family agrees with the transition plan and that the plan is implemented.

RN 2 plus years clinical experience
2 years inpatient acute hospital case management experience OR experience in either acute OR non-acute case management.

Required Certification/Registration

Current California RN License
Current BLS for Health Care Provider from American Heart Association.

Preferred Education/Experience/Specialized Skills/Certification

BSN highly desired.
Case Management experience preferred.
Case Management certification highly desired.
EPIC experience preferred.

At Scripps Health, you will experience the pride, support and respect of an organization that has been repeatedly recognized as one of the nation’s Top 100 Places to Work.

You’ll be surrounded by people committed to making a difference in the lives of their patients and their teammates. So if you’re open to change, go ahead and unlock your potential.

Three years of progressively more responsible professional library experience, with two years in a supervisory capacity.

 A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in library science, public administration, or related field. In addition, a Master’s degree in Library Science (MLS) from a college or university accredited by the American Library Association is required.

Possession of an appropriate, valid California driver’s license and a satisfactory driving record, which must be maintained as a condition of employment.

Meet The Team

Cisco is building the infrastructure foundation for the AI era, bringing together networking, security, observability, automation, and operations to help customers move AI from experimentation to enterprise-scale production. The Product Marketing organization plays a critical role in translating this innovation into compelling customer stories, differentiated positioning, and go-to-market execution.

Your Impact

You will lead cross-functional programs that strengthen how Cisco positions, communicates, and brings its portfolio to market. You will partner with Product Marketing, Product Management, Sales, Corporate Marketing, and other key stakeholders to advance high-impact initiatives, evolve product and portfolio messaging, and ensure Cisco’s value is clearly and consistently communicated to customers and partners. Your work will help connect Cisco’s strategy and innovation to compelling market narratives and go-to-market execution.

Success in this role requires a strong program leader who can translate strategic priorities into actionable programs, align diverse stakeholders, and manage complex initiatives from strategy through execution. You will establish program governance, drive clarity across priorities and dependencies, measure business outcomes, and identify opportunities to strengthen Cisco’s external presence. This is an opportunity to help shape how Cisco communicates its vision, differentiates its portfolio, and brings innovative solutions to market

What You’ll Do

In this role, you will be the driving force behind Cisco’s AI infrastructure portfolio, leading cross-functional, customer-facing programs from initial strategy through to successful execution. You will serve as a central partner across Product Marketing, Product Management, Sales, and Corporate Marketing, ensuring our go-to-market priorities are not only met but accelerated. By managing program plans, governance, risks, and dependencies, you will provide clear executive reporting and translate high-level strategic goals into measurable, real-world outcomes. As a highly organized leader who thrives in ambiguity, you will identify key opportunities to strengthen Cisco’s market presence and customer impact. Your ability to communicate effectively across technical and business audiences, combined with a data-driven, curious mindset, will be essential in navigating complex initiatives and delivering solutions that resonate with our customers and define our future in the AI space.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Marketing, or equivalent experience.

Experience supporting enterprise technology, AI, product marketing, or go-to-market programs.

Experience reviewing success measures and tracking business outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong communication and influencing skills across technical, business, and executive stakeholders.
Experience supporting Sr. Director, VP or SVP level leaders.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

CAMBA is a community of staff, volunteers, clients, donors, neighbors and partners who work together to build an inclusive New York City, where all children and adults have access to the resources and supports they need to thrive. We take a comprehensive approach by offering more than 180 integrated programs in: Education & Youth Development, Family Support, Job Training & Employment Support Services, Health, Housing, and Legal Services. We reach more than 73,000 individuals and families, including almost 13,000 youth. CAMBA serves a diverse cross section of New Yorkers from new mothers in Brownsville to job seekers in the Rockaways. More than half of our clients are immigrants and refugees from around the globe. Over 85% of our families are in living in poverty, reflecting the challenges faced by nearly 1.7 million New Yorkers today.

Hegeman Avenue Apartments
is a supportive/affordable housing development located in the Brownsville section of Brooklyn. Hegeman Avenue Apartments provide affordable housing for low-income working families up to 60% of Area Median Income along with 42 units set aside for formerly homeless individuals who are Population A (SPMI/NYNY III) eligible. CAMBA provides on-site supportive services including case management and 24/7 front desk security services. Amenities include a community room with a kitchen, a library/computer room, a tenant garden and laundry room.

Review all documentation establishing tenants' eligibility for program and make file copies.
Create and maintain tenant files.
Conduct initial intake and assessment of tenants and tenants' families' needs and periodic re-assessments.
In collaboration with tenants, prepare initial and periodic revisions of independent living plans including short-term and long-term tenant goals.

jobs.title: Rural Utah Outreach Program Specialist/Veterans Service Officer
jobs.description:
Are you a veteran looking for a meaningful opportunity to continue your service?

The Utah Department of Veterans & Military Affairs (DVMA) is seeking a dedicated, mission-driven Veterans Service Officer (VSO). In this role, you will act as a primary advocate, helping local veterans, military members, and their families navigate and secure the benefits they have earned.

About The Role

As a Veterans Service Officer, you will counsel, advise, and assist veterans and their dependents in obtaining county, state, and federal benefits. You will serve as both an advocate and a case manager, balancing complex caseloads with proactive community outreach.

Our ideal candidate is a veteran who understands the unique experiences of military life and can build strong partnerships to expand our outreach network across Severe, Sanpete, Carbon, Millard, Juab, Emery, Grant, Wayne, Piute, Garfield, and San Juan counties.

Position Information

Salary Range: $19.28 - $32.33
Status: Full-time
Schedule Code: B - Competitive Career Service (12 month probationary period)
Work Schedule & Travel: Requires regular travel across the service area and occasional holiday and weekend work for events.
Background Check: Employment is contingent upon obtaining and maintaining a security clearance, if needed.
Location: Richfield UT (Counties: Severe, Sanpete, Carbon, Millard, Juab, Emery, Grant, Wayne, Piute, Garfield, San Juan)
Recruiter: Jill Barela I jbarela@utah.gov I 385-202-4484
Application Deadline:08/12/2026
*This job posting may close at any time after the minimum advertising period of three (3) business days has passed, should a sufficient applicant pool be received. Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

Key Responsibilities

Client Advocacy & Case Management
Conduct Eligibility Assessments: Interview veterans and beneficiaries to evaluate their eligibility for various state and federal benefit programs under the Veterans Benefits Acts. Provide referrals when appropriate.
Manage Claims Processes: Prepare, submit, and track complex compensation and pension claims, ensuring all documentation is accurate and complete.
Set Clear Expectations: Educate claimants on their role in the application process, the scope of your support, and the legal framework governing VA decisions.
Maintain Confidentiality: Handle sensitive personal information with care, strictly safeguarding Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

Program Navigation & Education
Navigate Digital Platforms: Efficiently utilize VA.gov, Veterans.utah.gov, and related state and federal systems to process information.
Educate on State Benefits: Guide clients through state-specific veteran benefits, including tax abatements, Veteran Resource Centers, in-state tuition, legal assistance, state park passes, Veteran cemetery, State Veterans' Homes, First Times Homebuyer Program, Military Retirement Tax, while being familiar with partner programs like those offered by the Department of Workforce Services (DWS), etc.
Educate on Federal VA Benefits: Provide counseling on disability compensation, pensions, healthcare, Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E), burial benefits, housing assistance, etc.
Explain Complex Eligibility Criteria: Effectively communicate and clarify the statutory eligibility requirements established by the VA for granting Service-Connected Disability (SCD), Burial Benefits, and Survivor Pension/Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC).

Outreach & Communication
Community Representation: Attend meetings and serve on committees alongside VA staff and local community partners to promote DVMA programs.
Inquiry Resolution: Respond to inquiries from the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), and congressional offices in a clear, timely, and professional manner.
Position requires occasional weekend work.

Qualifications

To be considered for this role, you must meet the following criteria:

Certification: Ability to become a VA-certified Veterans Service Officer (VSO) within six (6) months of hire.
Training: Ability to successfully complete all mandatory state and federal training programs within designated timelines.
Driving Record: A valid driver's license and a clean driving record (demonstrated by a recent DMV printout).
Technical Proficiency: Strong computer skills, including experience with Microsoft Windows, Word, Excel, web navigation, and email systems.
Crisis Management: Ability to work effectively under high-pressure conditions—utilizing active listening and de-escalation techniques—while maintaining emotional composure, personal well-being, and professional effectiveness.

Preferred Qualifications

Veteran Status: Preference will be given to veterans and disabled veterans who received an honorable discharge.
Local Knowledge: Residence within Richfield in Sevier County is highly preferred due to the nature of the work and to facilitate outreach across the assigned region.
Education: College education preferred, but will consider High School diploma or equivalent with military service

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

In order to be successful, the following are essential:

Veterans Benefits Expertise: Working knowledge of VBA requirements and procedures for processing diverse veteran benefit claims.
Interpersonal Communication: Ability to active-listen, communicate information clearly, and deliver engaging public presentations or training sessions.
Professional Writing: Ability to draft clear, concise correspondence and formal responses to government agencies.
Collaboration & Supervision: Ability to work collaboratively with community agencies and functionally supervise program volunteers.

Why You Should Join Our Team

At our core, we believe that those who serve our country deserve top tier support when they come home. Our vision is clear: Make Utah the best state in the nation to perform military missions and be recognized as a premier location for Veterans, service members and their families to live and succeed.

When you join us, you’re not just taking a job—you’re becoming a dedicated advocate and innovator. We work across government, private, and non-profit sectors to open doors to available benefits, build a statewide community that honors service and expand opportunities on Utah’s military installations. Guided by five core principles—Respect, Awareness, Access, Responsiveness, and Effectiveness—we are building a culture where your service is valued and your mission continues. If you’re ready to channel your drive, integrity, and passion for service into making Utah the best place in the nation for Veterans and their families, we want you on our team.

The Agency

For more information on the Utah Department of Veterans & Military Affairs, click here .

Benefits At a Glance

Exceptional Health Coverage: We offer some of the most competitive medical premiums in the industry, including comprehensive family plans with very low out-of-pocket costs and HSA options.
Retirement Choice: Flexibility between a 10% employer-paid 401(k) (no match required) or a Pension/401(k) Hybrid plan.
Generous Paid Time Off: 12 paid holidays per year plus 8 hours of combined leave (4 annual and 4 sick) accrued each pay period.
Dental & Vision: Multiple high-quality plan options to fit your needs.

The mission of the Colorado Coalition for the Homeless is to work collaboratively toward the prevention of homelessness and the creation of lasting solutions for homeless and at-risk families, children, and individuals throughout Colorado. The Coalition advocates for and provides a continuum of housing and a variety of services to improve the health, well-being, and stability of those it serves.

Our Philosophy of Service:
We believe all people have the right to adequate housing and health care. We work to remove the barriers that restrict access to these rights. Society benefits when adequate housing and health care are available to everyone. We create lasting solutions to homelessness by:

Honoring the inherent dignity of those we serve, affirming their capabilities and fostering their hope that a better life is possible.
Building strong, caring and trauma-informed communities through the integration of housing, health care and supportive services.
Advocating for social and racial equity, inclusion and diversity, and challenging the status quo in partnership with our workforce members and those we serve.
Achieving excellence through continuous quality assurance, innovation and professional development.
Using resources judiciously and effectively.

The Case Manager
I works collaboratively alongside case managers, supervisors, integrated health team members, and community-based partners across the organization to promote long term solutions for families, children, and individuals experiencing homelessness or who have formerly experienced homelessness. This role is responsible for developing and implementing care plans, coordinating services and resources, monitoring client progress, providing advocacy and support, facilitating referrals to other services, and maintaining case documentation and data collection. Client Care Management and Support Services are grounded in motivational interviewing, stages of change, strengths-based case management, housing first, harm reduction, cultural responsiveness, and trauma-informed care. jobs.description:
Company Description
West Central Alabama AHEC (WCAAHEC) is a 501(c)(3) non-profit, community-based organization located in Greene County in Eutaw, Alabama. Established in 2013, WCAAHEC was created to increase access to healthcare services in West Alabama through education and prevention initiatives. The organization focuses on improving healthcare access via workforce development, expanding the capacity and services of existing providers and healthcare networks, and enhancing health outcomes through community-based interventions. WCAAHEC also emphasizes sustainable population health management, working collaboratively with partners and communities to support long-term health initiatives.
JOB SUMMARY

Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Community Outreach Coordinator will serve as the primary point of contact for day-to-day program case management and coordination of services that improve mental health status, well-being, financial stability, and social supports that reduce risk of suicide for eligible veterans and active-duty service members in Greene, Hale, and Tuscaloosa county. The coordinator is responsible for program oversight, participant screenings, referral coordination, detailed documentation, and collaboration with the regional veterans affairs(VA) office and community organizations. The coordinator collaborates with leaders and content experts to establish priorities, execute strategies, and implement programs. The individual in this role is expected to identify opportunities to improve outreach activities, strengthen community partnerships, and increase program effectiveness , using critical thinking and problem-solving skills to ensure program success.

Summary of Responsibilities;

▪       Assess on an ongoing basis the needs of eligible individuals and their families for suicide prevention services,
▪       Coordinate the provision of suicide prevention services with VA services for which eligible individuals are also eligible,
▪       Tailor (i.e., provide individualized) suicide prevention services to the needs of eligible individuals and their families.
▪       Seek continuously new sources of assistance to ensure the continuity of suicide prevention services for eligible individuals and their families as long as the eligible individuals are determined to be at risk of suicide.
Responsibilities will include but are not limited to
;
▪       Conducting outreach and screenings, coordinating with community partners and the VA, supporting participant enrollment activities, maintaining communication with referral partners
▪       Maintaining regular contact with participants to monitor progress, identify new needs, and help ensure veterans remain connected to services and support that promote wellbeing, stability, and reduced suicide risk
▪       Documenting program activities, coordinating educational and outreach events, and assisting with program reporting and implementation activities.
▪       Working directly with participating veterans and family members to assess needs, coordinate referrals, assist with accessing VA healthcare and benefits, connect participants to supportive services and public benefits
▪       Providing follow-up contacts, monitoring participant progress, and supporting ongoing case management activities to help address barriers affecting wellbeing and stability.
▪       Referrals and service coordination through established communication channels, warm hand-offs, follow-up contacts, and regular coordination with participating organizations to help ensure veterans and family members are connected to appropriate services and resources in a timely manner
▪       Conducting ongoing monitoring and periodic site visits to help ensure services are delivered as intended and that vendors and collaborating organizations remain aligned with program requirements and objectives
▪       Utilizing VA-required screening and assessment tools to identify suicide risk factors, behavioral health concerns, barriers to care, and other service needs
▪       Working with participants to develop realistic, achievable goals and identify steps needed to connect them to appropriate services and resources
▪       Connecting veterans to VA healthcare, behavioral health services, benefits, housing resources, employment assistance, transportation support, or other community resources

Education

Bachelor’s degree required in Social Work, Social Services, Public Health, Healthcare Administration, Behavioral Health, Human Services, Business Administration, or a closely related field. Master’s degree in a related field preferred.

Work Experience

Minimum Two (2) years of process improvement and project coordination experience. Experience in case management is strongly desired. Preferred Two (2) years of working veterans, active-duty service members, and/or families. Experience working with Microsoft Excel and Word and G-Suite. Federal and state grant administrative experience preferred.

Required Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities

▪       Experience managing multiple projects and collaborating with leaders, community partners, and multidisciplinary teams.
▪       Ability to develop and implement programs and processes that support suicide prevention and improve access to services for eligible Veterans and active-duty service members.
▪       Strong organizational, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
▪       Excellent communication, facilitation, conflict resolution, and relationship-building skills.
▪       Ability to work effectively with all populations, including Veterans, military families, healthcare providers, and community organizations.
▪       Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor information to different audiences.
▪       Social media savvy (including but not limited to LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok)
▪       Ability to identify obstacles to care, develop practical solutions, and lead initiatives without direct supervisory authority.
▪       Experience building partnerships, conducting community outreach, and promoting suicide prevention resources and services.

Salary range is low to mid 40s with fringe benefits including medical, vision, and dental insurance, cell phone allowance, holidays, and paid time off. Extensive in-state travel and some out of state travel required. This is not
a remote position. The West Central AL AHEC main office is located in Eutaw, AL.(Greene County).

Additional duties as required

Ability to meet with the patient, their physicians, other healthcare providers, attorneys, advisors/clients, and coworkers

Are you passionate about creating a safer, more supportive community? SARC (The Sexual Assault/Spouse Abuse Resource Center) is seeking dedicated individuals to join us in our mission to be Harford County’s lifeline for victims and survivors of domestic violence, sexual violence, child abuse, and stalking.

Position Description:

Responsible for all direct services and community education offered under SARC’s Human Trafficking (HT) Regional Navigation program. Core work hours Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30pm. May require evenings and weekends in order to attend events or facilitate training.

Position Description:

Responsible for all direct services and community education offered under SARC’s Human Trafficking (HT) Regional Navigation program.  Core work hours Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30pm. May require evenings and weekends in order to attend events, facilitate training, or provide crisis advocacy/accompaniment on a rotating on-call schedule.

         Evaluate the needs of the Human Trafficking program and suggests appropriate changes and/or additions to the program procedures- following approval of the Chief.

         Maintain a good working relationship and open communication with stakeholders and Harford County Agencies that provide referrals to the Program.

         Facilitate all intakes and complete HT assessments for the program.

         Provide in-person crisis intervention that includes safety planning, emergency response, basic living needs, and victim advocacy.

         Provide ongoing support, comprehensive case management, and advocacy to all identified survivors.

         Provide survivor advocacy and accompaniment to emergency medical care, medical forensic exams, law enforcement interviews, and prosecution interviews.

         Act as the direct conduit for required HT notifications from law enforcement and the Department of Social Services, and referrals or queries from local schools, local hospitals/medical facilities, the Child Advocacy Center, and other community partners.

         Provide community education, training, and staff information tables to raise awareness and understanding about human trafficking, sexual violence, dating violence, and domestic violence.

         Provide technical assistance to partner agencies on service provision to survivors of trafficking.

         Coordinate, directly provide and/or ensure warm handoffs to services that address identified needs such as safety planning, housing, mental health/substance abuse, medical care, self-care, legal services, basic needs, etc.

         Coordinate in-house legal and counseling services for clients.

         Identify, establish and strengthen partnerships with organizations that will assist survivors of human trafficking in areas of workplace development, education, long-term housing, etc.

         Assist the Chief of Programs and Grants Coordinator in required quarterly reports to GOCCP.

         Attend the Human Trafficking Coalition monthly meetings and other related local and statewide collaborative efforts or trainings as assigned by Chief of Programs.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, or a related field plus 2 years of relevant experience is minimally required. A Master’s degree in Social Work, Psychology or a related field is preferred, and additional relevant experience is strongly favored. The position requires knowledge of psychosocial services and a wide range of skills including trauma-informed care, comprehensive case management, public speaking, local resource access, and crisis response. Description

The Cabinet for Health and Family Services (CHFS) is home to most of the state's human services and health care programs, including the Department for Medicaid Services, the Department for Community Based Services the Department for Public Health, the Department for Aging and Independent Living and the Department for Behavioral Health, Developmental and Intellectual Disabilities. CHFS is one of the largest agencies in state government, with nearly 8,000 full- and part-time employees located across the Commonwealth focused on improving the lives and health of Kentuckians.

The Department for Public Health's Office of Vital Statistics (OVS) is the only official system of vital statistics in the Commonwealth. OVS Program Coordinators Interpret laws, regulations, policies and procedures for OVS programs. They request and collect program data, edits and analyzes data, and write comprehensive program status reports. They perform in depth analysis of program support needs and make recommendations to policy and procedures. They review records and reports submitted by program recipients or agency staff for compliance with legal, regulatory or policy standards. They respond to programmatic inquiries from the general public, governmental officials, or other jurisdictions. There is a continued need to communicate procedural or program changes to program staff, contractors, recipients, and other interested parties. There is a need for continued development of systems in support of 3 distinct core functions. OVS is comprised of dedicated individuals who provide excellent customer service.

The Program Coordinator professionally interprets and applies laws, rules, regulations (KRS 213/KAR 901:5) and office policies applicable to the administration of the Office of Vital Statistics (OVS).

Provide professional communications to stakeholders.
Provides necessary training to staff and agencies accurately and timely.

Strong presentation skills.

Who We Are:
CAMBA is a community of staff, volunteers, clients, donors, neighbors and partners who work together to build an inclusive New York City, where all children and adults have access to the resources and supports they need to thrive. We take a comprehensive approach by offering more than 180 integrated programs in: Education & Youth Development, Family Support, Job Training & Employment Support Services, Health, Housing, and Legal Services. We reach more than 72,000 individuals and families each year at our 100 locations, including 10,000 youth. CAMBA serves a diverse cross section of New Yorkers from new mothers in Brownsville to job seekers in the Rockaways. More than half of our clients are immigrants and refugees from around the globe. Over 85% of our families live in poverty, reflecting the challenges faced by nearly 1.7 million New Yorkers today.

Hegeman Avenue Apartments is a supportive/affordable housing development located in the Brownsville section of Brooklyn. Hegeman

Avenue Apartments provide affordable housing for low-income working families up to 60% of Area Median Income along with 42 units set aside for

formerly homeless individuals who are Population A (SPMI/NYNY III) eligible. CAMBA provides on-site supportive services including case management

referred by the New York City Human Resources Administration (HRA). On-site support services for these units are also provided by CAMBA through a

contract with the New York State Office of Mental Health (OMH) under the NY/NY III Program.

All public areas of the project will be fully handicapped accessible

Reports To: Program Director

Location: 212 Hegeman Ave. Brookyn, NY 11212

Maintain professional relationships with clients and client confidentiality.
Practice Universal Precautions/Standard Protocol & Procedures.
Comply with any and all Federal, State, City and CAMBA security and privacy polices intended to protect the security and privacy of individually identifiable health information.
Communicate with peers in other CAMBA programs on issues related to client progress and best program practices.
Work with direct reporting staff to set staff performance targets in accordance with contract requirements.
Develop and document all program activities.
Interface with the Director of Housing Operations or the property management company to ensure the building is clean and operating efficiently.
Participate in start up activities including marketing and lease up, program evelopment and implementation etc.
Access community resources for clients.
Ensure that all apartment vacancies are filled within 4-6 weeks.
Oversee all program operations and manage direct reporting program staff and their subordinates.
Develop and implement Quality Assurance measures to ensure quality service delivery to clients.
Ensure that all client files and program files are kept in compliance with CAMBA's and funder's standards.
Coordinate and supervise programmatic activities of direct reporting staff. Observe direct reporting staff.
Conduct program progress reviews with staff.
Prepare, review and ensure the accuracy and timeliness of, contract reports and statistical information for both CAMBA management and funder use.
Analyze program and demographic data to make programmatic improvements. Oversee onsite and organize offsite training opportunities for professional development of staff.
Confer with the Senior Program Director and/or other CAMBA management staff as needed regarding programmatic and personnel issues.
Complete incident reports when required Participate in staff/funder/outside agency meetings as requested.
Review and sign time sheets.
Prepare performance appraisals for direct reporting staff.
Immediately report to the appropriate Senior Program Director any: monitoring visits or funders' events; significant events; any incident that might subject CAMBA to liability.
May interact with funders.
May make hiring and firing recommendations to appropriate Senior Program Director/Executive Vice-President (in consultation and agreement with Human Resources).
May have direct client service/program responsibilities in addition to the above.
Tasks may be modified, expanded and/or assigned over time

Bachelor’s Degree (BA or BS) and two years of applicable experience, and/or equivalent experience

This position serves as a Capital Program Management and Contract Administration Lead responsible for supporting the delivery of water and wastewater infrastructure projects through procurement oversight, consultant management, contract administration, JOC program support, and implementation of standardized project management practices. jobs.title: Financial Success Program Manager
jobs.description:
Welcome to VCU, a world unlike any other.

VCU is a public research university unlike any other, dedicated to serving the needs of students and patients. We tackle difficult challenges others can’t or won’t. We’re home to creativity, teaching, discovery and healing. Our location in the heart of downtown Richmond, Virginia, means the nonstop energy of our city ignites our innovation and provides unlimited opportunities for our students.

The VCU Financial Success Center by Virginia Credit Union (FSC) is dedicated to helping our community achieve financial success. It aims to increase the prominence of financial instruction, research, programming and monitoring among the VCU community.

The FSC provides the VCU community with free personal and professional financial education, including assistance and counseling on budgeting, saving, credit, student loan repayment, career transitions and more. It supports all aspects of financial success through solutions, education and research-oriented financial programs that help reduce debt and increase overall financial confidence.

This isn't business as usual. It's innovation at work. We are unlike any business school you've ever seen.

Join us. You can be unstoppable here.

Position Summary

The VCU Financial Success Center by VACU is seeking highly motivated and qualified candidates to apply for the role of Financial Success Program Manager. The primary purpose of the Financial Success Program Manager is to guide and counsel students as it relates to personal finance matters including options to pay for college, financing options with persistence to graduation, budgeting, building credit, and minimizing debt. The Financial Success Program Manager will play an active role in creating a culture of care as a part of the student’s success team by fostering meaningful relationships with students and campus partners to enhance the students’ successful university experience.

The Financial Success Program Manager is expected to maintain a high level of professionalism, accountability and collaboration with various VCU campus partners and departments. The Financial Success Program Manager is expected to assist in coordinating and administering the VCU Financial Success Center’s financial well-being and education services while providing individual financial counseling and outreach programming. The Financial Success Program Manager will work closely with the Executive Director, Graduate Assistant(s) and student staff to help manage the operations of the VCU Financial Success Center by VACU.

Please Note: This is a “restricted position” with funding for one year (with potential for renewal). Employment eligibility after one year is dependent upon successful performance and continued funding.

Duties & Responsibilities

Student Mentorship & Staff Supervision

Recruit, hire, train, and supervise a cohort of undergraduate and graduate Peer Financial Coaches.
Conduct regular one-on-one supervision, observations, and performance feedback sessions to ensure coaching quality and adherence to Financial Success Center standards.
Manage scheduling, workflow, and daily operations for the peer coaching team.
Collaborate with student staff to execute key programmatic initiatives and outreach efforts.
Foster a collaborative, student-centered team environment.

Financial Coaching & Education

Provide individualized financial coaching for VCU students, including maintaining a caseload of one-on-one appointments, including students enrolled in the Career Bridge program and first-generation, low-income student populations.
Develop and facilitate financial education programming for students across a range of backgrounds.
Deliver engaging workshops and presentations for classrooms, student organizations, campus partners, and community organizations.
Collaborate with university partners, including the Career Bridge project care team and other campus stakeholders, to provide holistic student support.
Contribute to the university's strategic goals related to student financial wellness.

Outreach, Marketing & Communications

Lead the development and implementation of outreach strategies that increase awareness and engagement with Financial Success Center services.
Oversee the Center's monthly newsletter and support ongoing digital communications, including social media, marketing campaigns, branding, and other communication materials.
Coordinate financial wellness tabling and outreach at high-traffic events across the MCV and Monroe Park campuses.
Represent the Financial Success Center at university and community events to strengthen partnerships between VCU and the Richmond community.

Data Analysis, Operations & Program Development

Analyze appointment, outreach, and program participation data to identify trends, assess program effectiveness, and inform continuous improvement.
Compile outreach and program metrics and provide regular reports on program activities and outcomes.
Develop, update, and maintain physical and digital educational resources and operational materials.
Attend professional development workshops, webinars, conferences, and training to remain current on financial wellness trends and best practices.
Lead or support special projects and strategic initiatives that advance the mission of the Financial Success Center, the School of Business, and university financial wellness efforts.
Work on special projects and initiatives as needed to support the School of Business.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Financial Planning, Finance, Accounting, Business, Higher Education, Counseling, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience
Two (2) or more years of professional experience in financial wellness, financial education, financial coaching, higher education, student affairs, or a related field.
Demonstrated knowledge of personal financial planning, financial literacy, and financial coaching principles.
Experience developing, facilitating and coordinating programs, projects, events, or outreach initiatives
Strong quantitative, analytical, organizational, and project management skills, including experience collecting, analyzing, and reporting program data to inform decision-making and continuous improvement.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex financial concepts clearly
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends and travel locally within the Richmond area.
Demonstrated ability to work in and foster an environment of respect, professionalism and civility with a population of faculty, staff, and students from all backgrounds and experiences, or a commitment to do so as a faculty member at VCU.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in Financial Planning, Business, Higher Education, Counseling, Student Affairs, or a related field.
Experience supervising, mentoring, training, or leading student employees, peer educators, interns, or professional staff.
Experience managing financial wellness, financial literacy, or student success programs in a higher education setting.
Experience developing strategic outreach, marketing, and engagement initiatives, including digital communications and social media.
Experience with assessment, program evaluation, and continuous improvement practices.
Professional certification such as Certified Financial Planner™ (CFP®), Accredited Financial Counselor® (AFC®), or similar credential.
Experience working with college students and applying evidence-based financial education and coaching strategies to improve student success.

Additional Information

Priority will be given to candidates who submit their applications by August 12th.

All full-time university staff are eligible for VCU’s robust benefits package that includes comprehensive health benefits, paid annual and holiday leave, generous tuition benefits, retirement planning and savings options, tax-deferred annuity and cash match programs, employee discounts, well-being resources, abundant opportunities for career development and advancement, and more.

Typical Schedule: Monday - Friday, 40 hours per week, and may require periodic weekend and evening hours. This position is in-person on the VCU Monroe Park Campus in Richmond, VA.

The VCU Financial Success Center by VACU is committed to the growth and professional development of its team members and will provide opportunities to foster a culture of learning and career development.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S without the need for employer sponsorship

jobs.description:
About Carrier

Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure safe transport of food, lifesaving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow on Carrier social media at @Carrier.

About This Role

The Program Manager for Data Centers initiatives is responsible for managing and optimizing the aftermarket performance and satisfaction for their key account. This role is responsible for developing strategic relationships to ensure their data center needs are met effectively, and driving performance improvements. The Aftermarket Account Program Manager acts as a liaison between the client and internal teams to address issues, implement solutions, and deliver high-value services.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and maintain strong relationships with clients, understanding their aftermarket needs and objectives.
Act as the primary point of contact for key accounts, providing exceptional customer service and support.
Conduct regular meetings with clients to review aftermarket performance, address concerns, and identify opportunities for improvement.
Monitor and analyze the performance of data center aftermarket services and solutions provided to clients.
Utilize data analytics and reporting tools to track key performance indicators (KPIs) and service levels.
Identify trends, areas for improvement, and opportunities for optimization to enhance client satisfaction and operational efficiency.
Address and resolve client issues or concerns promptly, coordinating with internal teams to ensure effective solutions.
Manage escalations and work to resolve complex or critical problems that impact client performance or satisfaction.
Develop and implement strategic account plans to align with clients’ business goals and requirements.
Propose and execute initiatives to enhance service delivery, drive innovation, and support clients’ evolving needs.
Prepare and present regular performance reports and reviews to clients, highlighting achievements, challenges, and future plans.
Maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to account performance, service levels, and client interactions.
Ensure that services and deliverables are provided in accordance with contractual agreements and service level agreements (SLAs).

Required Qualifications

High School Diploma or GED
4+ years of experience supporting program management, or project management, sales, operations or application engineering.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelors’ degree
Experience supporting high impact, cross-functional projects.
Demonstrated technical aptitude and/or learning agility.
Demonstrated experience leading and executing complex projects.
Effective management and influence of non-direct reporting resources.
Strong ability to work with diverse, cross-functional project teams to achieve high levels of performance in a dynamic, changing environment.
Proven ability to manage large programs, executing with speed and exhibiting a bias for action.
Ability to communicate effectively in written and verbal format across a wide audience.
Demonstrated skill in using project management tools.
Knowledge of HVAC and service industries are a plus.
Ability to travel up to 60%

Pay Range

The annual salary for this position is between $117,500.00 - $234,500.00 annually. Factors which may affect pay within this range include, but are not limited to, skills, education, experience, and other unique qualifications of the successful candidate.

Other Compensation

This position is entitled to short-term cash incentives, subject to plan requirements.

Benefits

Employees are eligible for benefits, including:

Health Care Benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision; Wellness incentives
Retirement Benefits
Time off and Leave: Paid vacation days, up to 15 days; paid sick days, up to 5 days; paid personal leave, up to 5 days; paid holidays, up to 13 days; birth and adoption leave; parental leave; family and medical leave; bereavement leave; jury duty leave; military leave; purchased vacation
Disability: Short-term and long-term disability
Life Insurance and Accidental Death and Dismemberment
Tax-Advantaged Accounts: Health Savings Account; Health Care Spending Account; Dependent Care Spending Account
Tuition Assistance

Work with us | Carrier Corporate
.

Carrier EEO Statement and Accommodations Process

jobs.title: H.O.P.E. Program -Case Manager
jobs.description:
Are you looking for a purpose-driven career? At Metrocare, we serve our neighbors with developmental or mental health challenges by helping them find lives that are meaningful and satisfying.

Metrocare is the largest provider of mental health services in North Texas, serving over 55,000 adults and children annually. For over 50 years, Metrocare has provided a broad array of services to people with mental health challenges and developmental disabilities. In addition to behavioral health care, Metrocare provides primary care centers for adults and children, services for veterans and their families, accessible pharmacies, housing, and supportive social services. Alongside clinical care, researchers and teachers from Metrocare’s Altshuler Center for Education & Research are advancing mental health beyond Dallas County while providing critical workforce to the state.

Job Description

The H.O.P.E. (Helping Others Progressively Evolve) Program Case Manager provides intensive, participant-centered case management for adults involved in the criminal justice system who have behavioral health, substance use, and co-occurring needs. The Case Manager serves as the primary point of contact for Dallas County Criminal Justice participants enrolled in the H.O.P.E. Program.

The Case Manager conducts comprehensive assessments, develops individualized service plans, coordinates access to behavioral health and community-based services, and builds collaborative treatment teams that include participants, family and natural supports, behavioral health providers, probation officers, attorneys, peer recovery specialists, and community partners. The Case Manager promotes participant engagement, accountability, recovery, and successful community reintegration through coordinated, evidence-based case management.

This position requires a professional who can build trusting relationships while maintaining clear professional boundaries and supporting the expectations of a specialty program. Using knowledge of Social Drivers of Health, Trauma-Informed Care, Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care, Harm Reduction principles, and Motivational Interviewing, the Case Manager coordinates services that address participants' behavioral health, substance use, housing, employment, education, transportation, healthcare, recovery support, and other social service needs while promoting long-term stability and reducing recidivism.

Responsibilities

Serve as the primary point of contact for H.O.P.E. Program participants, providing ongoing support, advocacy, engagement, and care coordination throughout program participation.
Conduct comprehensive behavioral health, psychosocial, and resource assessments to identify participant strengths, needs, barriers, and recovery goals.
Develop, implement, monitor, and update individualized, person-centered service and recovery plans that support treatment participation and successful completion of program requirements.
Utilize Motivational Interviewing, strengths-based practices, trauma-informed care, and crisis intervention techniques to promote engagement, accountability, behavior change, and recovery.
Maintain regular contact with participants through office visits, telephone contacts, community visits, and collateral contacts as appropriate.
Coordinate behavioral health treatment, substance use treatment, psychiatric services, medical care, medication management, peer recovery support, and other community-based services.
Facilitate referrals, coordinate appointments, monitor attendance, and follow up to ensure successful linkage with recommended services.
Coordinate continuity of care during transitions between incarceration, residential treatment, outpatient treatment, hospitalization, community supervision, and recovery support services.
Assist participants in addressing Social Drivers of Health, including:
Housing
Food security
Transportation
Employment
Education
Government identification
Health insurance
Public benefits
Financial assistance
Recovery support services
Support participants in developing independent living skills, problem-solving abilities, relapse prevention plans, healthy coping skills, and natural support systems.
Monitor participant compliance with treatment recommendations, psychiatric appointments, medication management, counseling sessions, recovery meetings, and program requirements.
Attend multidisciplinary staffing meetings and specialty program sessions.
Provide timely verbal and written updates regarding participant progress, treatment engagement, compliance, barriers, behavioral concerns, and recommendations.
Collaborate with judges, attorneys, probation officers, treatment providers, psychiatrists, peer specialists, housing providers, employers, educational institutions, and community partners to promote participant success.
Assist the multidisciplinary team in identifying appropriate incentives, therapeutic interventions, and graduated responses to participant behavior.
Coordinate transition planning and community reintegration services for participants entering or leaving residential treatment, incarceration, hospitalization, or other levels of care.
Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with behavioral health providers, substance use treatment programs, hospitals, housing agencies, educational institutions, employers, and community organizations.
Identify service gaps and advocate for resources that improve participant outcomes and continuity of care.
Maintain accurate, objective, and timely documentation of assessments, participant contacts, referrals, service plans, treatment progress, outcomes, and program-related activities within the electronic health record.
Maintain confidentiality in accordance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, agency policies, and program requirements.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Compentencies

The competencies listed here are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

Demonstrates integrity, professionalism, accountability, and ethical decision-making in accordance with agency policies, professional standards, and applicable federal and state laws.
Strong analytical, critical thinking, organizational, problem-solving, and time-management skills with a commitment to continuous quality improvement.
Ability to assess participant needs, evaluate clinical information, develop individualized service plans, and coordinate appropriate behavioral health and community services.
Knowledge of behavioral health, substance use disorders, co-occurring disorders, recovery support services, Social Drivers of Health, and community resources.
Knowledge and application of Trauma-Informed Care, Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing, Recovery-Oriented Systems of Care, and Person-Centered Planning.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to build rapport, maintain professional boundaries, and effectively engage justice-involved individuals.
Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams, criminal justice partners, treatment providers, and community agencies.
Strong advocacy skills with the ability to identify barriers, coordinate services, and promote recovery-oriented outcomes.
Demonstrates cultural humility, adaptability, resilience, professionalism, and respect for diverse populations.
Maintains accurate documentation and confidentiality in accordance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, agency policies, and program requirements.

Qualifications

Required Education, Experience, Licenses, and Certifications

Bachelor's Degree from an accredited college or university with a minimum of 30 credit hours in a social, behavioral, or human services field and two (2) years of experience providing case management, behavioral health services, substance use treatment services, or criminal justice services.
Acceptable coursework includes psychology, social work, counseling, sociology, rehabilitation, nursing, medicine, human growth and development, educational psychology, gerontology, physician assistant studies, early childhood intervention, and related behavioral sciences.
Valid Texas Driver License.
Reliable transportation.
TB Test, CPR, First Aid, and SAMA completed within 30 days of hire.
TAC web-based training.
Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) trainings completed within the first year of employment.

Preferred Education, Experience, Licenses, And Certifications

Master's Degree from an accredited college or university in Social Work, Counseling, Psychology, Behavioral Health, Criminal Justice, Public Health, or another related behavioral science field.
Experience working with:
Adult Specialty Courts
Mental Health Courts
Drug Courts
Behavioral Health Systems
Substance Use Treatment Programs
Justice-Involved Populations
Community Supervision
Co-occurring Disorders
Qualified Mental Health Professional (QMHP)
Licensed Master Social Worker (LMSW)
Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW)
Licensed Professional Counselor Associate (LPC Associate)
Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC)
Certified Case Manager (CCM)
Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor (LCDC)

jobs.title: Specialist Program Manager
jobs.description:
What We Are Looking For

The 3D Systems team in Littleton, Colorado is seeking an experienced Specialist Program Manager with a strong technical background and proven project management expertise to lead strategic initiatives that support product onboarding, new product introduction (NPI), production process development, technology transfer, and continuous process improvement. This role requires a versatile leader who is equally comfortable managing complex, cross-functional programs as well as directly leading individual projects from initiation through successful completion.

The ideal candidate will possess the ability to oversee a portfolio of interconnected initiatives while seamlessly transitioning into a hands-on project management role when business priorities require focused execution. Whether driving product realization efforts, equipment implementation, process validation, manufacturing transfers, operational improvement initiatives, or customer onboarding projects, this individual will ensure projects are delivered on time, within scope and budget, and aligned with organizational objectives.

Success in this role requires exceptional organizational and leadership skills, the ability to influence cross-functional teams in a matrixed environment, and a proactive approach to identifying and mitigating risks. The Senior Program Manager will partner closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory, Commercial, and Customer teams to ensure successful execution while fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.

What's in it for You!

Competitive Pay: $129,300- $193,900 per year. Our employees are the best part of our company. We want you to feel valued, appreciated, and included. Because of this, we make sure your hard work is recognized.
Paid Leave (US ONLY): Enjoy time away from work with Company paid holidays and a flexible working schedule through our paid time off (PTO) policy.  Yep, you read that correctly. We are a Company that values you and makes sure you take time for yourself.
401(k): Prepare for a secure retirement with our 401k plan, which includes an employer matching contribution.
Comprehensive Health & Wellness Plans: We want to be here for our employees throughout all stages of life, which is why we offer a wide range of resources, information, and support during your career with us.
Global Team: With our state-of-the-art corporate headquarters in Rock Hill, South Carolina, our global team has a presence across more than 15 countries worldwide. Experience a workplace comprised of talented individuals who are passionate about serving our customers and each other.
Innovative Culture: Innovation is at the heart of what we do! Since our founding in 1986 by Chuck Hull, the inventor of 3D printing, we have continuously pushed the boundaries of what is possible with additive manufacturing. When you join 3D, you will have the opportunity to work with cutting edge technology in an innovative and collaborative culture
Talent Development: At 3D Systems, we invest in talent programs to support employees with opportunities to grow, contribute, develop, and thrive in their careers.
Connection & Engagement Opportunities: We strive to cultivate an environment where our diverse global workforce can connect and thrive. Our Employee Resource Group program, Employee Recognition program, and 3D Gives Back program, are just a few examples of how you will be empowered to build connections, celebrate wins, and make a meaningful impact.

What You Will Do

Lead project, program, and portfolio management activities throughout the lifecycle of assigned initiatives, including project planning, execution, cross-functional coordination, milestone management, risk mitigation, budget and schedule oversight, and regular communication with leadership, customers, and key stakeholders.
Design, implement, standardize, and continuously improve Project Management Office (PMO) processes, tools, governance, and software solutions to establish consistent project execution across multiple business units.
Manage complex cross-functional programs while also serving as the hands-on project manager for individual initiatives, ensuring deliverables are completed on time, within scope, within budget, and in compliance with quality and regulatory requirements.
Lead lower- to moderate-complexity projects, including new product introduction (NPI), product onboarding, technology transfer, manufacturing process validation, equipment implementation, supplier integration, operational improvements, and customer-driven technical initiatives.
Develop and maintain project documentation, including project charters, scope statements, work breakdown structures, integrated schedules, resource plans, communication plans, risk registers, decision logs, action trackers, and project closeout documentation.
Establish and facilitate effective project governance through recurring team meetings, milestone reviews, customer status updates, executive reporting, action item management, decision tracking, and escalation processes.
Serve as the primary customer-facing project leader by coordinating technical discussions, managing customer communications, and translating customer, quality, validation, certification, and manufacturing requirements into executable project plans.
Provide technical leadership for technology transfer, manufacturing implementation, validation, and continuous improvement initiatives involving additive manufacturing, subtractive manufacturing, post-processing, inspection, and related production processes.
Evaluate existing manufacturing methods, operational workflows, project risks, and process constraints to identify opportunities that improve efficiency, quality, scalability, and overall business performance.
Collaborate with Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, and external suppliers to develop manufacturing solutions, implement new equipment, support installation and qualification activities, and ensure successful project execution.
Develop, coordinate, and execute verification and validation (V&V) protocols, engineering studies, technical reports, and supporting documentation required for manufacturing readiness, product realization, and regulatory compliance.
Communicate project status, technical findings, risks, key decisions, and deliverables to customers, executive leadership, and cross-functional stakeholders through clear and effective written and verbal communication.
Lead implementation activities supporting manufacturing readiness, including visual work instructions, engineering change orders (ECOs), process documentation, training programs, production handoffs, and operational transition plans.
Ensure compliance with 3D Systems' Quality Management System (QMS), Design Controls, Change Control processes, Product Realization procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
Facilitate project and program reviews at key milestones, providing executive-level visibility into project health, risks, resource requirements, mitigation strategies, and overall progress.
Lead formal project closeout activities, including completion of all contractual and technical deliverables, documentation, lessons learned, stakeholder acceptance, production readiness, and successful transition to Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, or Sustaining Engineering teams.
Support the preparation, compilation, and review of technical documentation required for domestic and international regulatory submissions, customer qualifications, and product certifications, as applicable.

What You Will Bring

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Project Management, or a related technical discipline required; equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience will be considered.
Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM), or other relevant project/program management certification preferred. Candidates with equivalent project or program management experience are encouraged to apply.
Demonstrated success managing both complex cross-functional programs and individual technical projects, including planning, execution, stakeholder management, risk mitigation, documentation, reporting, and project closeout.
Proven ability to seamlessly transition between strategic program leadership and hands-on project management, personally driving lower- to moderate-complexity projects while overseeing broader organizational initiatives as business priorities evolve.
Minimum of 4–5 years of experience supporting manufacturing operations within a regulated environment, preferably under FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, ISO 9001, or similar quality management systems.
Experience working in additive manufacturing within a production environment is required. Familiarity with technologies such as Direct Metal Printing (DMP), Stereolithography (SLA), Selective Laser Sintering (SLS), or other additive manufacturing platforms is highly desirable.
Strong technical foundation in manufacturing engineering principles, including process development, product realization, process optimization, design support, statistical analysis, testing and inspection methodologies, supplier collaboration, structured problem solving, engineering change management, and process validation.
Experience developing and maintaining project documentation, including integrated schedules, dashboards, action registers, risk logs, project metrics, stakeholder communications, and project closeout documentation.
Experience planning, executing, and documenting Verification and Validation (V&V) activities, including protocol development, execution, reporting, and technical documentation.
Working knowledge of quality systems, inspection methodologies, metrology, and manufacturing quality processes is preferred.
Experience supporting downstream manufacturing operations, production readiness, technology transfer, or manufacturing implementation activities is a plus.
Proficiency with project management and reporting tools such as Smartsheet, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Project, Power BI, or similar software platforms.
Excellent organizational, analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively influence and collaborate across cross-functional teams and all levels of the organization.
Demonstrated commitment to delivering exceptional customer service while balancing technical requirements, business objectives, quality expectations, and project timelines.
Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 25% as business needs require.

We'll be accepting application until August 12, 2026

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to, among other things, race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, genetic information, marital status, gender identity or national origin or because he or she is an individual with a disability or a disable veteran, Armed Forces service medal veteran (referred to collectively as "protected veterans").
